key_insight: CG-OMatG uses an equivariant Riemannian flow model to generate molecular crystal structures by hierarchically predicting rigid-body molecule placements and lattice parameters.
engineering_relevance: This could accelerate crystal structure prediction and polymorph screening for organic materials by reducing the search space for low-energy candidate packings.
method: Coarse-grained hierarchical generative model for molecular crystals
Treats molecules as rigid bodies and learns centroid positions, orientations, and lattice parameters
Adds policy-gradient reinforcement learning to bias generation toward low-energy structures
evidence_signal: The model was trained on OMC25 and CSD subsets and evaluated on the CSP blind test benchmark using COMPACK packing-similarity against experimentally determined crystals.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of coarse-graining, rigid-body assumptions, and the representativeness of training data for unseen polymorphs.
paper_title: Riemannian Flow Models with Reinforcement Learning for Molecular Crystal Structure Prediction
